narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Jonas briskly, including every speech introduction and aside.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking to his prophet; commanding, then patient and gently questioning.

shipmaster.name: The ship master
shipmaster.note: Pagan captain of the ship, urgent and alarmed in the storm.

mariners.name: Mariners
mariners.note: The pagan crew; frightened, questioning Jonas, then crying out to the Lord.

jonas.name: Jonas
jonas.note: The reluctant prophet, son of Amathi; resigned in the storm, fervent in prayer, sullen and angry at Ninive's pardon.

1.t: Now the word of the Lord came to Jonah, the son of Amathi, saying:

2.t: Arise and go to Ninive, the great city, and preach in it: For the wickedness thereof is come up before me.

3.t: And Jonah rose up to flee into Tharsis from the face of the Lord, and he went down to Joppe, and found a ship going to Tharsis: and he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them to Tharsis from the face of the Lord,

4.t: But the Lord sent a great wind to the sea: and a great tempest was raised in the sea, and the ship was in danger to be broken.

5.t: And the mariners were afraid, and the men cried to their god: and they cast forth the wares that were in the ship, into the sea, to lighten it of them: and Jonah went down into the inner part of the ship, and fell into a deep sleep.

6.t: And the ship master came to him and said to him:
Why art thou fast asleep? rise up call upon thy God, if so be that God will think of us that we may not perish.

7.t: And they said every one to his fellow:
Come and let us cast lots, that we may know why this evil is upon us.
And they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonah.

8.t: Tell us for what cause this evil is upon us, what is thy business? of what country art thou? and whither goest thou? or of what people art thou?

9.t: I am a Hebrew, and I fear the Lord, and the God of heaven, who made both the sea and the dry land.

10.t: And the men were greatly afraid, and they said to him:
(For the men knew that he fled from the face of the Lord: because he had told them.)

11.t: What shall we do with thee, that the sea may be calm to us?
for the sea flowed and swelled.
11.q: read as the narrator's explanation ("flowed and swelled", past tense), not part of the mariners' question

12.t: take me up, and cast me into the sea, and the sea shall be calm to you: for I know for my sake this great tempest is upon you.

13.t: And the men rowed hard to return the land, but they were not able: because the sea tossed and swelled upon them.

14.t: And they cried to the Lord, and said:
We beseech thee, O Lord let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for thou, oh Lord, hast done as it pleased thee.

15.t: And they took Jonah, and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from raging.

16.t: And the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and sacrificed victims to the Lord, and made vows.
